trajectory_summary: This call opens with an unusually engaged customer who quickly surfaces several real objections (roof aversion, cost skepticism, prior bad experience with Sunrun) but resolves each one through direct conversation and ultimately self-proposes the appointment. The bill-document collection stalls badly because the customer's utility does not display kWh usage, but the rep pivots to a square-footage-based estimate rather than losing the appointment. The call ends with a booked appointment, a captured bill amount, and unresolved formatting confusion (AM/PM) that should be double-checked before the follow-up text goes out.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown; based on the transcript this is clearly 'booked' — a specific day (Thursday) and time (2:30 PM) were agreed, with the rep committing to a confirmation text. The AM/PM stumble at 12:20-12:29 is a minor execution risk, not enough to downgrade to tentative, since both parties align on PM by the end of the exchange.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Button-up mechanics: explicit date/time restate + missing handshake
primary_coaching_focus.quote: And you said that oh, wait a minute. 02:30 would be the time I want. I don't want AM. My PM is preferred.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment is the entire output of this call, and the AM/PM confusion plus the absence of a clear one-hour-block statement, no-driving/computer instruction, or an explicit 'is that fair?' handshake are all schema-required button-up elements that were skipped. A confirmed, unambiguous appointment protects the setter's paycheck (setters are paid on sits, not bookings) — tightening this mechanic directly reduces no-show risk.

key_moments.quote: Hi. This is Joe with Ion. Joe Joe, hi. This is Lisa Chris Smith. Kevin called and left me a message.
key_moments.stewart_read: The intro is garbled and appears to be a callback-to-a-missed-message scenario rather than a clean outbound intro; the rep explains the cut-off phone number as the reason for calling, which is a reasonable improvised legitimacy anchor, but it is not the clean company+reason template.

key_moments.quote: And here's my problem. It's a brand new house with a brand new roof. It's only four months old.

The rep validates ('That's a good deal') rather than flipping the frame — e.g., a brand-new roof is actually the ideal, lowest-risk time to install solar since there's no re-roof needed for 25+ years.
